title: Design Authentication Manager
description:
# Design Authentication Manager

An authentication system issues tokens. A token generated at `currentTime` expires exactly at `currentTime + timeToLive`. A token can be renewed only while it is still unexpired; renewal changes its expiry to `currentTime + timeToLive`.

Implement the `AuthenticationManager` class:

* `AuthenticationManager(int timeToLive)` stores the lifetime shared by all tokens.
* `void generate(String tokenId, int currentTime)` creates a new token with expiry `currentTime + timeToLive`.
* `void renew(String tokenId, int currentTime)` renews the token only if it exists and its current expiry is strictly greater than `currentTime`; otherwise the call is ignored.
* `int countUnexpiredTokens(int currentTime)` returns how many tokens have expiry strictly greater than `currentTime`.

If a token expires at time `t`, it is already expired for any operation whose `currentTime` is `t`. Therefore both `renew` and `countUnexpiredTokens` must treat `expiry == currentTime` as expired.

In operation examples, the first array lists operations and the second lists their argument lists, paired by index and executed left to right. The first operation constructs the object; later operations use that same object. Outputs align by index too: constructors and void methods produce `null`; an empty argument list `[]` means no arguments.

## Example 1

**Input:**
["AuthenticationManager", "renew", "generate", "countUnexpiredTokens", "generate", "renew", "renew", "countUnexpiredTokens"]
[[5], ["aaa", 1], ["aaa", 2], [6], ["bbb", 7], ["aaa", 8], ["bbb", 10], [15]]

**Output:**
[null, null, null, 1, null, null, null, 0]

**Explanation:**
`renew("aaa", 1)` is ignored because `aaa` does not exist. `generate("aaa", 2)` makes `aaa` expire at time `7`, so it is counted at time `6`. `renew("aaa", 8)` is ignored because `aaa` already expired at time `7`. `generate("bbb", 7)` makes `bbb` expire at time `12`; `renew("bbb", 10)` extends it to time `15`. At time `15`, `bbb` is exactly expired and is not counted.

## Constraints

* `1 <= timeToLive <= 10^8`
* `1 <= currentTime <= 10^8`
* `1 <= tokenId.length <= 5`
* `tokenId` consists only of lowercase letters.
* All calls to `generate` use unique `tokenId` values.
* The `currentTime` values across all function calls are strictly increasing.
* At most `2000` calls will be made to all functions combined.

examples.explanation: At time 15, token bbb has expiry exactly 15, so it is not unexpired.

solutions.name: HashMap Expiry Scan Baseline
solutions.timeComplexity: O(1) for generate and renew, O(n) for count
solutions.description:
## Approach
Store the latest expiry time for each token in a `HashMap`. `generate` writes `currentTime + timeToLive`; `renew` updates only when the saved expiry is strictly greater than `currentTime`; `countUnexpiredTokens` scans all saved expiries and counts those still greater than `currentTime`.

## Key Insight
A token whose expiry time equals `currentTime` is already expired, so every validity check must use `expiry > currentTime`. This baseline keeps the rule obvious before optimizing cleanup.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(1) expected for `generate` and `renew`, O(n) for `countUnexpiredTokens`
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: FIFO Expiry Events with Version Check
solutions.description:
## Approach
Keep the latest expiry time in a map and append every generated or renewed expiry event to a FIFO queue. Because all `currentTime` values are strictly increasing and `timeToLive` is fixed, newly appended expiry events are also in nondecreasing expiry order. Cleanup pops expired events from the queue front.

## Key Insight
Renewal creates stale older events for the same token. An expired queue event should delete the token only when its expiry still equals the token's latest expiry in the map; otherwise it is an old version and must be ignored.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(1) amortized per operation because each event is enqueued and dequeued once
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: LinkedHashMap Expiry Order Cleanup
solutions.description:
## Approach
Use a `LinkedHashMap` whose iteration order is the token expiry order. Generation appends a new token. Renewal removes the token and inserts it again at the end with a later expiry. Cleanup repeatedly examines the first entry and removes expired tokens.

## Key Insight
Since `currentTime` is strictly increasing and `timeToLive` is fixed, each successful generate or renew creates an expiry later than every previously created expiry. Re-inserting renewed tokens keeps the front of the map as the earliest possible expiry.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(1) amortized per operation after cleanup costs are charged to removed tokens
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: TreeMap Expiry Buckets
solutions.timeComplexity: O(log n) per generate or renew plus expired removals
solutions.description:
## Approach
Maintain a map from token to its latest expiry and a `TreeMap` from expiry time to all tokens expiring at that time. Cleanup removes the earliest expiry bucket while its key is less than or equal to `currentTime`. Renewal moves one token from its old expiry bucket to a new one.

## Key Insight
The `TreeMap` makes expiry order explicit even when many tokens share the same expiry time. The token-to-expiry map is still required so that renew can find and move exactly one token.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(log n) per generate or renew, plus O(r log n) total cleanup over r removed expiry buckets
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: PriorityQueue Expiry Heap with Version Check
solutions.timeComplexity: O(log n) per generated or renewed event
solutions.description:
## Approach
Store the latest expiry in a map and push every expiry event into a min-heap ordered by expiry. Cleanup polls heap entries whose expiry is no later than `currentTime`, deleting the token only when the heap entry still matches the latest map version.

## Key Insight
The heap route does not rely on FIFO append order. It is a more general event-scheduler model, and the same version check protects renewed tokens from stale earlier heap entries.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(log n) for each generated or renewed event, with each stale event also polled once
- Space Complexity: O(n)

tests.description: Canonical sequence: nonexistent renew is ignored, exact-expiry renew fails, and exact-expiry count excludes the token.
Expiration boundary: currentTime equal to expiry is already expired.
Renewing just before expiry extends the token beyond the original boundary.
A stale old expiry event from a renewed token must not delete the new version.
Renewing a nonexistent token and renewing an exactly expired token are both ignored.
Multiple tokens can overlap, renew independently, and expire in separate cleanup batches.
High currentTime values and maximum-length token ids still obey the exact expiry boundary.
Cleanup must handle several exact-expiry checks while later renewal remains valid.
